'''Robert Joseph Young''' FRS (born 29 May 1948)<ref name=whoswho/> is a British [[materials science|materials scientist]] specialising in [[polymer]]s and [[Composite material|composites]].<ref>{{cite book | last1=Kinlock | first1 = A.J. | last2 = Young | first2=R.J. | title=Fracture Behaviour of Polymers Paperback | publisher=Springer | year=2014 | isbn=978-9401715959 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=Young | first=Robert | title=Introduction to polymers | publisher=CRC Press | location=Boca Raton | year=2011 | isbn=978-0-8493-3929-5 }}</ref> He is Emeritus Professor of Polymer Science and Technology at the Department of Materials and [[National Graphene Institute]] at the [[University of Manchester]].<ref name="FRS" />

== Education ==
Young was educated at [[St John's College, Cambridge]], where he received his [[Master of Arts]]<ref name="whoswho" /> and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degrees.<ref name=youngphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=Deformation mechanism in crystalline polymers|first= Robert Joseph|last=Young|date=1972|url=https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/250659|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.478386}}|website=repository.cam.ac.uk|oclc=183326728}}</ref><ref name=orcid>Robert Joseph Young {{ORCID|0000-0001-6073-9489}}</ref>

== Research and career==
Young has published over 330 research papers which have been cited over 37,000 times, leading to a h-index of 91.<ref name=orcid/><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> He is known for research on the relationships between the structure and mechanical properties of polymers and composites. A particular focus of his work has been the study of how materials such as [[carbon fibre]]s and [[spider silk]] [[Deformation (engineering)|deform]] at the molecular level. He has also studied [[Carbon fiber reinforced polymer|carbon-fibre composite]]s, [[carbon nanotube]]s and the deformation of [[graphene]] — a one-atom thick sheet of [[carbon]].<ref name="FRS" /> Among his work on polymer-graphene composites, one important result elucidated for the first time the relationship between composite reinforcement and matrix modulus.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Young |first1=Robert J. |last2=Liu |first2=Mufeng |last3=Kinloch |first3=Ian A. |last4=Li |first4=Suhao |last5=Zhao |first5=Xin |last6=Vallés |first6=Cristina |last7=Papageorgiou |first7=Dimitrios G. |title=The mechanics of reinforcement of polymers by graphene nanoplatelets |journal=Composites Science and Technology |date=January 2018 |volume=154 |pages=110–116 |doi=10.1016/j.compscitech.2017.11.007|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In his research, Young made a novel use of [[Raman spectroscopy]]. In this technique, [[laser]] light is shone onto a material and the wavelength and intensity of the resulting [[Scattering|scattered]] light is measured and analysed. The changes in the light relate to changes in [[bond length]] between the atoms of the molecules in the material when the material is deformed.<ref name="FRS" />

He has also co-authored the widely used textbook: ''Introduction to Polymers''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Young |first1=Robert J. |last2=Lovell |first2=Peter A. |title=Introduction to Polymers |year=2011 |url=https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.1201/9781439894156/introduction-polymers-robert-young-peter-lovell |doi=10.1201/9781439894156|isbn=9781439894156 }}</ref>

=== Awards and honours ===
Young received the 2011 Leslie Holliday Prize and the 2012 Swinburne Medal from the [[Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining]], and delivered the Swinburne Lecture in 2013.<ref name="FRS" /> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2013|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2013]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/robert-young-12582|title=Robert Young|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2013|website=royalsociety.org}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{quote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=2016-11-11 }}}}</ref> His certificate of election reads: {{centered pull quote|Robert Young is one of the world's foremost scientists and his innovative research has transformed our understanding of the relationships between structure and mechanical properties in polymers and composites. He has developed a theoretical framework to describe the role of dislocations in the [[plastic deformation]] of [[semi-crystalline polymer]]s and identified new [[toughening]] mechanisms. He subsequently pioneered the use of Raman spectroscopy to study deformation micromechanics in fibres at the molecular level. He has demonstrated that this approach can be extended to the deformation of carbon-nanotubes and graphene nano-composites and has proven that [[continuum mechanics]] is still applicable at the nano-scale<ref name="frsCitation">{{cite web |url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%27EC%2F2013%2F44%27%29 |title = EC/2013/44: Young, Robert Joseph|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=22 December 2017|author=Anon|year=2013}}</ref>}}
